record.context_brief: explicit constructions of calibrated minimal submanifolds
record.original_question: Determine whether every calibrated minimal submanifold can be constructed by an explicit method, analogous to the Weierstrass representation, that produces a large class of minimal submanifolds in Euclidean space R^n or on the sphere S^n.

evidence.quote: Can all calibrated minimal submanifolds be produced by an explicit method (similar to the Weierstrass representation method) which exhibit a large class of minimal submanifolds in R^n or S^n?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $n \geq 3$. A smooth closed differential $k$-form $\varphi$ on Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^n$ (or on the round sphere $S^n$) is called a calibration if, at every point, its restriction to every oriented tangent $k$-plane is at most the Riemannian volume of that plane. An oriented $k$-dimensional submanifold $M$ is said to be calibrated by $\varphi$ if $\varphi$ restricted to each tangent space of $M$ equals the volume form of $M$. Every calibrated submanifold is volume-minimizing in its homology class, hence in particular minimal.

Recall the classical Weierstrass representation: every simply connected minimal surface in $\mathbb{R}^3$ admits a conformal parametrization
$$X(\zeta) = \mathrm{Re} \int_{\zeta_0}^{\zeta} \left( \tfrac{1}{2}(1-g^2)\, f,\ \tfrac{i}{2}(1+g^2)\, f,\ f g \right) dz,$$
where $f$ is a holomorphic function and $g$ a meromorphic function on a domain in $\mathbb{C}$, satisfying suitable compatibility conditions. This formula gives an explicit parametric construction producing a large class of minimal surfaces from free holomorphic data.

Question: Does there exist an explicit construction, analogous to the Weierstrass representation, that produces every calibrated minimal submanifold of $\mathbb{R}^n$ (and of $S^n$) from free analytic/holomorphic data, and which exhibits a large class of such submanifolds in arbitrary dimension and codimension?
artifact.status_search_result: Partial Weierstrass-type representations exist for special classes of calibrated submanifolds (e.g., special Lagrangians, associative/coassociative submanifolds, holomorphic curves) and recent work constructs new explicit families using complex-valued harmonic morphisms and eigenfunctions. However, no general explicit construction producing all calibrated minimal submanifolds of $\mathbb{R}^n$ or $S^n$ analogous to the Weierstrass representation is known; the underlying PDEs are generally too complicated for explicit solution. The general question appears still open.

status_evidence.title: Minimal Submanifolds via Complex-Valued Eigenfunctions
status_evidence.snippet: Complex-valued harmonic morphisms are used to study minimal submanifolds of codimension two; every regular fibre is a minimal submanifold.
status_evidence.claim: Recent partial techniques exist but no general Weierstrass-type construction for all calibrated submanifolds.

status_evidence.title: A Weierstrass Representation for Minimal Surfaces in 3-Dimensional Manifolds
status_evidence.snippet: A general Weierstrass representation formula exists for simply connected immersed minimal surfaces in an arbitrary Riemannian manifold, though the PDEs involved are generally too complicated to find explicit solutions.
status_evidence.claim: Generalizations exist but explicit solutions are generally unattainable, supporting that the general construction problem remains open.
